skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Automates browser sessions through inference.sh, including navigation, element interaction, screenshots, video recording, file uploads, proxies, and page JavaScript execution.
skill.summary: Run agent-guided browser automation with snapshots, screenshots, video, proxies, and reusable shell workflows.
skill.author: inference-skills

security_audit.summary: Many static hits are false positives from Markdown code fences, relative documentation links, example URLs, and harmless /dev/null redirection. Confirmed risk remains significant because the skill runs an external browser automation CLI, supports screenshots, videos, file uploads, arbitrary page JavaScript, authenticated sessions, and SOCKS proxies. Additional semantic risks include cookie extraction guidance and proxy rotation for rate-limit avoidance.

remediation.issue: Screen capture, video recording, and file upload can expose sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for screenshots, videos, and uploads, and document redaction or recording-disable steps for sensitive workflows.

remediation.issue: Cookie extraction guidance can leak session material.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie-printing examples or replace them with safer session verification patterns that do not expose cookie values.

remediation.issue: Proxy rotation is framed as rate limit avoidance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove anti-abuse language and limit proxy examples to authorized geo-testing, corporate access, or compliance testing.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary JavaScript execution can read or change authenticated page state.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit authorization warnings and examples that avoid reading cookies, tokens, or private DOM data.

remediation.issue: Executable shell templates run external browser automation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add preflight checks for target URL, CLI identity, output directory, recording state, and explicit cleanup before running templates.

1. **Open** - Navigate to URL, get `@e` refs for elements
| `open` | Navigate to URL, configure browser (viewport, proxy, video recording) |
| `snapshot` | Re-fetch page state with `@e` refs after DOM changes |
| `interact` | Perform actions using `@e` refs (click, fill, drag, upload, etc.) |
| `screenshot` | Take page screenshot (viewport or full page) |
| `execute` | Run JavaScript code on the page |
| `close` | Close session, returns video if recording was enabled |

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Agent Browser
content.value_statement: Manual browser tasks slow research, testing, and operations work. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code repeatable browser sessions with snapshots, actions, screenshots, and videos.
actual_capabilities: Open URLs and return compact page snapshots with @e element references.
Click, fill, select, check, drag, upload, scroll, wait, go back, and navigate by URL.
Capture viewport screenshots, full-page screenshots, and optional session videos.
Execute JavaScript on the current page and return the result.
Configure viewport size, user agent, HTTP proxies, SOCKS proxies, and proxy credentials.
Use included shell templates for forms, authenticated sessions, and content capture.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated CLI session before use.
Element references can expire after navigation or dynamic page changes.
Screenshots and videos are not automatically redacted for secrets or personal data.
Browser actions can affect real accounts and sites, so authorization is required.

use_cases.title: Validate Browser Flows
use_cases.description: Run form, login, and navigation checks while collecting screenshots or video evidence.

use_cases.title: Capture Web Research
use_cases.description: Open public pages, extract visible text, collect links, and save page screenshots for review.

use_cases.title: Automate Operations Tasks
use_cases.description: Repeat authorized browser workflows in admin tools after confirming target sites and credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this URL in a new browser session, show the visible interactive elements, and explain which element refs matter for the next step.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to this form, identify each required field, fill it with the provided test data, submit it, and verify the result page.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Record the browser workflow, perform these steps, capture a full-page screenshot at the final state, and summarize what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Authenticated Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use an authorized authenticated session to complete this workflow. Avoid recording sensitive fields, refresh refs after navigation, and close the session when done.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and capture the key interactive elements.
output_examples.output: A short page summary, the current title and URL, a screenshot reference, and the main buttons, links, and form fields available for action.

output_examples.input: Submit a test contact form and verify success.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step result showing which fields were filled, whether the submit action succeeded, the final page state, and a screenshot for evidence.

output_examples.input: Record a settings workflow for documentation.
output_examples.output: A completed session video, a final screenshot, and a concise summary of the navigation path and changed setting.

best_practices: Use only authorized sites, accounts, and credentials for browser automation.
Refresh snapshots after navigation, form submission, or dynamic page changes.
Disable video recording when credentials, tokens, personal data, or internal records may appear.
anti_patterns: Do not use proxy rotation to bypass rate limits, access controls, or site policies.
Do not print cookies, passwords, tokens, or session data into logs or captured artifacts.
Do not upload local files unless the target site, file path, and permission are explicit.

faq.question: Does this skill need another CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on the inference.sh CLI and uses the agent-browser app through that CLI.

faq.question: Can it interact with logged-in pages?
faq.answer: Yes, but only with authorized credentials and careful handling of cookies, screenshots, and videos.

faq.question: Can it scrape websites?
faq.answer: It can extract visible text and links from pages, but users must follow site terms and rate limits.

faq.question: Does it support file uploads?
faq.answer: Yes. It can upload local files to file input elements when explicit file paths are provided.

faq.question: Why do element refs stop working?
faq.answer: Refs can change after navigation or page updates. Take a fresh snapshot before the next action.

faq.question: Is video recording safe for sensitive workflows?
faq.answer: Use caution. Recordings can capture credentials, personal data, or internal pages unless recording is disabled.
